relations.rationale: Nell's past race ranking has no bearing on the group settling in under the stars.
Zeno being oldest of the five is consistent with and supports the claim that Zeno is older than Dara by a couple of years.
Zeno's age relative to Dara has no connection to Zeno pointing out a hawk.
Zeno's age difference from Dara is unrelated to when the group reaches the summit shelter.
Eli being on the same team as Zeno doesn't determine whether Mina is on that team or not, though it's compatible with Mina being on a different team.
Team membership of Eli and Zeno has no bearing on Dara setting up a camp stove.
Team membership of Eli and Zeno has no bearing on Nell unpacking sandwiches.
The trail leading to a rocky overlook supports the claim that the group paused for lunch there.
The trail description leading to the overlook is unrelated to reaching the summit shelter at sunset.
The trail's description has no direct bearing on the group settling in for the night under the stars.
Pausing at the overlook for lunch supports the idea that Dara set up a camp stove there for cooking.
Pausing for lunch supports Nell unpacking sandwiches as part of that lunch stop.
Stopping for lunch at the overlook is a separate earlier event and doesn't directly affect reaching the summit at sunset.
The lunch stop is unrelated to the group's later feelings of being tired but pleased.
Clouds rolling in could plausibly prompt the group to hurry toward the summit before weather worsens.
Clouds rolling in by early afternoon is compatible with and could support later reaching the summit at sunset after a full day.
Deciding to pick up the pace toward the summit supports the idea that they reach the summit shelter later that day.
Zeno pointing out the hawk directly explains why everyone stopped to watch it.
Stopping to watch a hawk earlier is unrelated to the later feeling of being tired but pleased.
Reaching the summit shelter at sunset supports the group feeling tired but pleased with their progress.
